items.title: Spend policy engine for agent-initiated payments
items.thesis: Agents can now check out on their own. Nobody can show you the policy layer that decides whether they should.
items.notes: Closest to the existing ACP POC. Ship after the ACP repo has a distinct angle so this reads as a layer, not a repeat.

items.title: Settlement reconciliation that balances to zero
items.thesis: Every payments team claims their recon is tight. Here is one that scores its own accuracy against injected breaks.
items.notes: First artifact. Break classes are injected with ground truth, so precision and recall are measured, not asserted.

items.title: Agent-to-agent credit with exposure limits and netting
items.thesis: If agents transact with each other all day, someone has to underwrite the float between them.
items.notes: Strongest novelty candidate. Needs a careful failure model: default, exposure, netting window.

items.title: Idempotency conformance suite for payment APIs
items.thesis: A payments API is not idempotent until a buyer can replay it and get the same answer. Most cannot.
items.notes: Shipped 2026-11-02, re-scored 4.60. Five implementations of one charge endpoint, 11 checks, named violation codes. store_after passes 6 of 11 with 7 excess charges; reserve passes 11 of 11. Promotion candidate on 4.6, but the HTTP adapter is what makes it useful to a buyer: promote after that.

items.title: Money allocation and FX rounding engine
items.thesis: The penny that goes missing when you split a payment across three parties is a real bug class, not a rounding footnote.
items.notes: Largest remainder allocation, preservation invariant, property based tests with Hypothesis.

items.title: Sanctions screening that cuts false positives
items.thesis: Screening is not a search box. It is entity resolution, and the cost of a false positive is a frozen customer.
items.notes: Shipped 2026-11-04, re-scored 4.60. 2400 customers, 26 entries, 36 injected true matches, 110 namesakes, fixed review budget. At 48 reviews: name-only caught 11 of 36 and spent 36 reviews on namesakes; entity resolution caught 33 with 11 namesakes and no ranking loss. 130 customers tie at the top name score, so the baseline queue is decided by a tie break. Three customers listed only under a kunya are missed by every policy, which caps recall at 0.917.

items.title: Authorization-rate aware payment routing
items.thesis: Routing on cost alone leaves money on the table. Routing on approval probability is where the margin is.
items.notes: Simulator with PSP-level latency, cost, and approval curves. Compare static rules, epsilon greedy, and Thompson sampling. Shipped 2026-11-06, re-scored 4.60. 50,000 synthetic transactions, 12 segments, hidden per-segment approval. Fee-only routing: 88.9% auth, 124.4 bps, $38,271 per 1,000. Reference: 94.3% auth, 151.3 bps, $39,802 (+4.0%). A three-line rule table recovers 4.06%, Thompson lands 0.06% below the reference, epsilon greedy 0.9% below. After a 0.90 logit shift against bravo on debit, rules lose 0.90% and all-history Thompson 1.25% against the reference, a 300 attempt window is level. Retry depth moves the gap from $2,689 to $1,151.

items.title: Subscription mandate simulator across rails
items.thesis: Card mandates, SEPA direct debit, and UPI autopay disagree about notifications, retries, and revocation. Most teams learn this in production.
items.notes: Shipped 2026-10-26, re-scored 4.75. Promotion candidate: the cross rail claim survives without the lab, but the UPI category exemptions need modelling first.

items.title: Chargeback representment state machine
items.thesis: Every dispute is a clock. The product is knowing which clock is running and what evidence still matters.
items.notes: Shipped 2026-11-11, re-scored 4.75, promotion candidate. 2,000 synthetic disputes, $356,862 disputed, $277,708 (77.8%) defensible, 40 analyst minutes a day. Ladder of five policies: status_only 21.3%, response_clock 66.5%, frees_added 73.8%, complete_evidence 77.3%, three_clock 94.0% ($260,905). Unlimited analyst time reaches 98.2%, so the staffing constraint is worth $11,682 and the queue ordering is worth more. 621 free wins ($153,411, 55.2% of the ceiling) need no evidence; the status tracker captured 6.4% of that. 563 of its 804 forfeits are fraud, because a 25 day sweep is longer than the 20 day fraud window. Contest precision 0.53 to 0.96, wasted minutes 2,385 to 934. All six bench checks pass, including budget and deadline binding checks.

items.title: Broker order, fill, and position reconciliation
items.thesis: Retail trading apps fail quietly at the seam between the broker, the exchange, and the books.
items.notes: Extends the Angel One repo into a reconciliation harness. Keep separate from recon to avoid theme repetition. Shipped 2026-11-09, re-scored 4.70, promotion candidate. 1,200 orders, 1,668 prints, 286 injected breaks in 8 classes. broker_only leaves 844 shares and 27.2 lakh rupees of drift and reports nothing; broker_vs_app flags 206 items at 0.43 precision and still leaves 1,424 shares off; stream_replay leaves 1,779 shares and 5.54 lakh of cash. tape_three_way names all 286 and the reconstructed book equals the tape, with the explained delta equality holding at a max gap of 0 across 6 symbols. Triage at 60 tickets covers 87 percent of rupee exposure by impact, 26 percent by arrival order.

items.title: Append only ledger with a provable close
items.thesis: Closing the books is a testable property, not a monthly meeting.
items.notes: Temporal queries, reversal only, period locks. Overlaps recon, sequence it after.

items.title: LLM underwriting judged by calibration, not vibes
items.thesis: An underwriting model is good when its probabilities mean something. Brier score does not care how confident the prompt sounded.
items.notes: Needs a pinned model and a recorded fixture set so results stay reproducible offline.

items.title: PAN vault with scoped detokenization
items.thesis: Storing the card number is easy. Proving who was allowed to read it, and why, is the product.
items.notes: Useful but the public version is well covered by vendor docs. Low novelty.

items.title: Bank statement to normalized ledger
items.thesis: Turning messy statements into clean entries is the unglamorous tax on every finance product.
items.notes: Crowded space, extraction quality is hard to prove without real statements, and real statements are PII.

items.title: Regulatory change watcher for PSD3, RBI, MiCA
items.thesis: Regulation moves monthly. Most teams read about it when a partner asks.
items.notes: Better as a newsletter than a repo. Fails the measured gate without an evaluation set.
